subject: Money
title: What Is a Bubble
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is a Bubble.

hook.text: In 2000, Pets.com sold dog food online, lost money on every sale, and was valued at $300 million. Then it was zero.

buildup.text: A bubble forms when asset prices far exceed intrinsic value, driven by speculation rather than fundamentals.

discovery.text: Economist Hyman Minsky identified three stages: displacement, euphoria, and panic. Every bubble follows this arc.

twist.text: Nobody knows they're in a bubble until it pops. During the ride, rising prices look like proof of value.

climax.text: Bubbles are recognized only in hindsight. That's what makes them dangerous and what makes them repeat.

punchline.text: If everyone sees it, it's not a bubble yet.

quiz.question: According to Minsky, what are the three stages of a bubble?
